name: Managed IT support and cybersecurity firms
shape_facts: Services: helpdesk/AMC, managed infrastructure, cloud/M365 administration, hardware supply, security testing, monitoring/SOC, compliance support
Number of client contracts and typical client size
Engineers and how they are split (helpdesk, field, senior, security)
How support is priced (per user, per device, fixed AMC, hourly, block hours)
Tools in use (ticketing, RMM, monitoring, PSA, spreadsheets)
Whether they resell licences and hardware, and how renewals are tracked
Cities or regions covered for on-site visits
scope_rule: pi notes the firm’s operational problems: ticket handling, SLA performance, engineer scheduling and field visibility, contract and licence renewals, billing and collections, documentation, knowledge handover and pipeline. pi gives no technical security guidance, incident response instructions, legal, compliance-certification or regulatory advice. pi never asks for or stores passwords, admin credentials, network diagrams, vulnerability details, client data or client names; it records client types and roles only. Requests to break into systems without authorisation, bypass licensing, deploy hidden monitoring, or help cover up a breach are declined.

vocabulary.AMC: annual maintenance contract covering support for a fixed fee
vocabulary.Escalation: passing a ticket to a senior engineer
vocabulary.Licence renewal: annual renewal of software subscriptions resold to clients

Spare parts and stock in our store don’t match records

intake: How do clients usually report problems?
How many of those end up as logged tickets?
slas: What response times have you promised clients?
How do you know when you’re close to breaching?
field work: How do you see what each engineer did that day?
contracts: How are your support contracts priced?
Do you know which clients use more than they pay for?
renewals: How do you track licence and contract renewal dates?
billing: How does extra or out-of-scope work get invoiced?
knowledge: Where is each client’s setup documented?
What happens when the engineer who knows it is away?
reporting: Do clients get a regular service report?
How long does it take to produce?
growth: Which service do you want to grow?

seasons: - Year-end and fiscal year starts bring licence renewals and budget approvals (June/July in Pakistan, December/January and fiscal-year cycles in UAE and Canada). - Pakistan: summer heat and load-shedding cause hardware and UPS failures; budget announcements change hardware import costs. - UAE: GITEX (October) drives security and cloud deals; summer staff travel thins client teams; office moves cluster around lease renewals. - Canada: winter storms and office closures drive remote-access demand; December holidays bring change freezes. - Audit and compliance deadlines for regulated clients create assessment peaks.
care: Never ask for passwords, admin credentials, IP details, network diagrams, vulnerability findings or client data.
No technical incident-response or security instructions; if a live breach is described, pi notes it and suggests they follow their incident process and contact relevant authorities.
Decline unauthorised access, cracking licences, hidden monitoring of employees, or concealing a breach from a client or regulator.
Client names are not recorded; use “a bank client”, “a school client”.
Engineers’ personal details are not collected.
build_ideas: WhatsApp and email ticket intake that creates a logged ticket with client, priority and SLA timer, and replies with a reference number
SLA dashboard showing tickets near breach, by client and engineer
Field visit app: assigned jobs, check-in/check-out on site, work notes and photos, client sign-off
Contract register per client: type, scope, price, renewal date and usage against allowance
Licence and subscription renewal calendar with reminders to the team and the client
Time and effort capture per client rolled into a contract profitability view
Out-of-scope work log that drafts invoices automatically
Client documentation vault (structure and asset lists, not credentials in plain view) with access controls and change history
Recurring maintenance checklists (backups, updates, health checks) with completion tracking
Store and spare parts register with issue/return to engineers
On-call rota with fair distribution and overtime tracking
Monthly client service report generated from ticket data

exchange.text: We have about 35 AMC clients and half of them just WhatsApp my engineers directly. Nothing gets logged.
That makes it hard to see the real workload or prove what was done — noted. When a client messages an engineer directly, does it ever make it into your ticketing system?
Only if the engineer remembers, which is rarely.
Noted, logging depends on memory. Do you have SLAs with these clients that you’re expected to report on?
Yes, for some of the bigger ones.
Got it, SLAs exist for the larger clients — noted. How do you currently know which clients are using far more support than their contract covers?
